problems.description: 84 naming violations (convention score 0.49): functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE across index.ts, cache-manager.ts and cache-manager.test.ts — the convention baseline for the whole project is being set badly in session 1.
Cognitive complexity +41 across only 11 functions (+7 SonarQube smells) in a greenfield session — functions are already too deeply nested/branched.
Duplications of 12.3% on the very first commit — copy-pasted logic is baked in before any refactor pressure exists.
+139 imports across 9 files (roughly 15 per file) in a scaffolding commit suggests a wide/tangled module surface or heavy re-export churn for the size of the app.
collectCoverageFrom excludes src/index.ts — the CLI entry point ships with no coverage requirement.

strengths: Correct greenfield scaffolding: jest + ts-jest + typescript configured cleanly with a dedicated testMatch/coverage setup.
Appropriate library selection for a static site generator (gray-matter for front matter, marked for rendering) and a declared ssg CLI bin.
Zero SonarQube bugs detected; no security or performance defects surfaced by static analysis.
package-lock.json committed, so installs are reproducible.
commit_reviews.summary: Sound greenfield architecture and tooling choices (jest/ts-jest, gray-matter/marked, zero bugs) but the commit sets a poor convention baseline (0.49 score, 84 naming violations) and starts accumulating technical debt immediately (12.3% duplication, +41 cognitive complexity) — neutral only because there is no prior state to regress.

problems.description: SonarQube delta reports +1 bug and +7 smells; cognitive complexity +32 across the 12 new functions, indicating template-rendering logic is materially more complex than the feature size warrants.
Duplication +5.9%: the five new test blocks each repeat the identical setup (writeFileSync markdown + new Generator({...})) instead of a shared helper.
Tests write to fixed in-repo paths (.test-gen-content/.test-gen-output/.test-gen-templates) that collide across parallel test runners and can leak artifacts if a test fails before afterEach cleanup.

Assertions are brittle — they depend on exact rendered strings like '' and '

Hello

', which break on any template whitespace/layout change.

103 imports added for the feature (bulk Handlebars surface + test imports); handlebars is a heavy CommonJS dep, now a runtime dependency pulling minimist, neo-async, source-map, uglify-js, and wordwrap into production.

strengths: Feature is well covered by tests: template-dir auto-creation, default layout fallback, custom layout via frontmatter, and partials all have dedicated cases.
Test lifecycle correctly cleans up temp dirs in afterEach, mirroring the existing test-file conventions.
Dependency classification is correct: handlebars added to dependencies and its formerly dev-only transitive deps reclassified accordingly.
Follows the established Generator config-object pattern (contentDir/outputDir/templatesDir), consistent with existing call sites.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-tested Handlebars templating feature that fits the generator's architecture and follows existing patterns, but adds one SonarQube bug, substantial cognitive complexity, and setup duplication that should be refactored.

problems.description: 84 naming-convention violations (PascalCase classes/interfaces, camelCase functions, UPPER_CASE constants) across index.ts, cache-manager.ts, cache-manager.test.ts; convention score 0.49 — the naming rules are violated pervasively, not edge cases

+45 cognitive complexity and +16 smells for a single integration feature is disproportionate to the change size (+601 lines) and suggests the dev-server/watch logic was added monolithically rather than decomposed

New cache-manager module introduced in the Session 3 integration commit — caching is the Session 5 scope (incremental builds + caching); premature abstraction risks rework during the Session 4 plugin refactor
Only cache-manager.test.ts accompanies the new code; no visible tests for the serve/watch/WebSocket reload path, which is the core deliverable of this session

strengths: Feature matches the Session 3 spec exactly: live-reload dev server using chokidar (file watching) and ws (WebSocket), serving from ./dist, without breaking the existing build command
Dependency hygiene is correct: chokidar/ws as runtime deps, @types/ws as devDependency, package-lock.json fully consistent (integrity hashes, versions, dev:true flags)
commit_reviews.summary: The commit delivers the on-spec live-reload dev server with the exact prescribed libraries (chokidar + ws) and clean dependency bookkeeping, but carries heavy maintainability debt — 84 naming violations (score 0.49), +45 cognitive complexity, +16 smells, and a premature cache-manager abstraction — so net it leaves the codebase worse on quality metrics.

problems.description: PluginLoader.createPipelineFromConfig drops the `options` field of `{plugin, options}` config entries — options are never passed to addPlugin, silently discarding per-plugin configuration; devServerOptions is also ignored whenever explicit plugins are supplied, a silent behavior change from the default pipeline.
Measured convention score 0.49 with 84 violations (functions should be camelCase, classes/interfaces PascalCase, constants UPPER_CASE) across index.ts and cache-manager.* — well below the repo's bar.
Duplicate data shapes: Page and ParsedPage are manually mapped in three places (fallbackGeneratePageHtml, index generation, main loop), so the two representations can drift when fields change.

generate() now delegates markdown→html rendering to plugin side-effects that set page.html, with a lazily-initialized template engine fallback; responsibility for a page's final content is split across the class and plugins, making the main path harder to reason about.
isPluginConfig uses an `any`-typed duck check ('plugin' in obj) that can misclassify plugin instances carrying a `plugin` property, and lacks the type narrowing to be safe.
New tests cover the default pipeline and custom plugins but not createPipelineFromConfig with plugin+options entries or the dev-server path — coverage that would have caught the dropped-options bug.

strengths: Lifecycle-hook plugin pipeline (start/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/end) is a clean, well-known SSG extensibility seam with sensible hook placement around the build.
Backward-compatible: plugins is optional and a default pipeline is created, so existing callers of Generator are unaffected.
Reuses the existing parser and template-engine modules rather than deleting them; the fallback keeps prior rendering behavior available.
Dedicated test file added covering both default-plugin and custom-plugin paths.
commit_reviews.summary: A structurally sound plugin-system refactor that adds a real extensibility seam and tests, but ships a loader bug (silently dropped plugin options), duplicative Page/ParsedPage handling, and a measured convention score of 0.49 with 84 violations — a neutral change that trades convention drift and latent debt for architecture; note the discrepancy between the good architectural design and the poor measured convention adherence.

problems.description: SonarQube delta shows +13 code smells and +39 cognitive complexity across the 4 new files — the cache/statistics logic is measurably more complex than what it replaced, with no compensating refactor.
frontmatterCache is typed Map<string, Record<string, any>> — the any type erases the frontmatter shape and invites downstream type drift.
CacheEntry.timestamp is written but never consumed for TTL/eviction — a latent dead field that suggests the expiry design is unfinished.
The timeSaved test relies on setTimeout(50ms) to assert timeSaved > 0 — a timing-based assertion that is flaky on fast CI runners and slow ones.
Redundancy between the persisted .ssg-cache.json manifest and the in-memory htmlCache/frontmatterCache Maps (which are not persisted): the two sources of cache state can diverge across a restart.

Mechanical convention score is 0.49 with 84 violations; however the specific violations cited (e.g. 'Classes should use PascalCase' for CacheManager/BuildStatistics) appear spurious, so the real adherence is likely higher than the measured 0.49.

strengths: Comprehensive test coverage — 215 lines exercising hash consistency, invalidation, manifest persistence, and cache clear, colocated per project convention (src/*.test.ts).
Zero new bugs and duplications down 4.0% per SonarQube.
Clean concern separation: CacheManager (cache state) and BuildStatistics (reporting) are distinct, focused classes.
commit_reviews.summary: A solid cross-cutting caching session with strong tests and no new bugs, but the low convention score (0.49 — possibly over-counting spurious violations) and +13 smells/+39 cognitive complexity warrant a flag.
